reasoning:
I found the bug: `collarLoop.at(0.5)` actually returns a Vector3 point, not a frame object, so calling `.at` on `throat` fails since Vector3 has no such method. I need to treat throat as a plain Vector3 instead, and I suspect `ropeLoop.at(...)` has the same issue.

The simplest fix is to wrap it like `const throat = { at: collarLoop.at(0.5) }` so all the existing `.at` references (medal, magatama, rod, tassels) still work without touching every call site. I double check whether t=0.5 on the loop actually lands near the throat/underside given the neck's tilt, and it seems roughly right. I scan the other frame-related calls (sashHit, cp.bone, bodySkin.loop, spine.joints) and they all look fine, so this minimal wrapper fix should be sufficient.
